article: Occupation, Detention, and the Legal Governance of War-Torn Territory

occupation_framework_matrix.rule_summary: Occupation generally turns on effective control over territory by hostile armed forces rather than formal annexation.
occupation_framework_matrix.key_authorities: Hague Regulations; Geneva Convention IV; ICJ Wall Advisory Opinion

occupation_framework_matrix.rule_summary: Occupying power must restore and ensure public order and civil life while respecting existing laws unless absolutely prevented.
Occupation does not transfer sovereignty and should not become a project of annexation, settlement, or permanent domination.
occupation_framework_matrix.key_authorities: Hague Regulations; Geneva Convention IV; ICJ 2024 OPT Advisory Opinion

occupation_framework_matrix.rule_summary: Protected persons retain humanitarian protections against coercion, collective punishment, deportation, transfer, and unlawful confinement.
Private property, public property, resources, and economic administration are constrained by usufruct, necessity, and humanitarian duties.
occupation_framework_matrix.key_authorities: Hague Regulations; Geneva Convention IV; Customary IHL

detention_framework_matrix.rule_summary: Combatants captured in international armed conflict may be detained as POWs and must receive Geneva Convention III protections.
Civilians in occupied territory may be interned only on imperative security grounds and with procedural safeguards.
All persons not taking active part in hostilities must be treated humanely in NIAC settings.
Sentencing and punishment require regularly constituted courts and indispensable judicial guarantees.
detention_framework_matrix.key_authorities: Common Article 3; Geneva Convention IV; Additional Protocols

detention_framework_matrix.rule_summary: ICRC visits and humanitarian access are central safeguards against disappearance, abuse, and unlawful detention.

protected_persons_matrix.protection_summary: Medical care and humane treatment must be provided without adverse distinction.
protected_persons_matrix.key_authorities: Geneva Conventions I and II; Customary IHL

protected_persons_matrix.protection_summary: POWs are protected against violence, intimidation, insults, reprisals, and unlawful punishment.
Civilians are protected against violence, coercion, collective penalties, deportation, transfer, and unlawful confinement.
NIAC detainees retain humane treatment and judicial guarantees under Common Article 3 and customary IHL.
protected_persons_matrix.key_authorities: Common Article 3; Additional Protocol II; Customary IHL

war_crimes_matrix.rule_summary: Deportation or transfer of protected persons from occupied territory may constitute a grave breach or war crime.
Unlawful confinement of protected persons may constitute a grave breach or war crime.
Transfer by an occupying power of parts of its own civilian population into occupied territory is prohibited and criminalized in the Rome Statute.
war_crimes_matrix.key_authorities: Geneva Convention IV Article 49; Rome Statute

war_crimes_matrix.rule_summary: Sentencing without indispensable judicial guarantees may constitute a war crime.
